rubric_scores.rationale: Measurability is strong, though judging 'boundary maintenance' in the rubric relies on qualitative expert evaluation[cite: 23].
The tasks directly map to the objectives: categorization for 'understand' and analysis/explanation for 'apply'[cite: 23].
Marking up real clause language and citing specific text is the authentic gold standard for contract review[cite: 23].
The progression from understanding risk taxonomies to applying them to novel clauses is perfectly aligned[cite: 23].
Identifying 'reading comprehension of legal-register prose' as a prerequisite is brilliant and essential to avoid confounding assessment results with basic reading deficits[cite: 23].
Module 1 establishes the conceptual taxonomy required to execute the procedural application in Module 2[cite: 23].
The use of worked examples to model the risk-analysis/legal-advice boundary is a very effective instructional choice[cite: 23].
Time is slightly tight (35 mins for the apply-level module), but manageable if the sample clauses are kept short and focused[cite: 23].
Zero scope creep. Highly focused on the specific desired performance[cite: 23].
Only trivial edits required to populate the actual taxonomy and clause content.

prerequisite_acceptance.notes: Both prerequisites are exceptionally well-chosen and safeguard the validity of the learning outcomes[cite: 23].

edit_effort.notes: The structure is excellent. The researcher merely needs to supply the specific legal text fixtures[cite: 23].
